 South Carolina early voting tops 800,000, sets pace for midterm record 
 South Carolina is on pace to shatter its previous midterm early voting record, with more than 830,000 ballots already cast ahead of Election Day. By Stephen Biddix Published : Oct. 30, 2026 at 6:12 PM EDT | Updated : 2 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google COLUMBIA, S.C. (WCSC) — South Carolina is on pace to shatter its previous midterm early voting record, with more than 830,000 ballots already cast ahead of Election Day.
 According to the South Carolina Election Commission, turnout has far exceeded the pace seen during the 2022 midterm election cycle. 
 Election Commission Executive Director Conway Belangia said turnout is already roughly double what the state saw four years ago and expects strong participation through the final days of early voting.
 “It is probably double what we saw four years ago, and we still have two solid days, and we know that Friday and Saturday will always be big turnout days just because it’s the last two days,” Belangia said.
 Greenville County leads the state in early voting with 83,212 ballots cast, followed by Charleston County with 78,759. Richland County ranks third with 73,786 votes, while Horry County has recorded 72,101 early votes. York County rounds out the top five with 47,196 ballots cast.
 The high turnout comes as several closely watched races are drawing national attention, including South Carolina’s U.S. Senate contest and multiple congressional races across the state.
 Belangia also used the opportunity to emphasize confidence in South Carolina’s election system, saying multiple safeguards are in place to ensure election security and accurate vote counts.
 “The voting system itself is never hooked to the internet, never hooked to a telephone line. It is run on the county level and protected on the county level as well as the state level, and so we’ve got multiple layers of protection,” Belangia said.
 Early voting in South Carolina ends Saturday at 6 p.m. Polls statewide will be open on Election Day, Tuesday, Nov. 3, from 7 a.m. until 7 p.m.
